newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds were lower late Wednesday following a downturn in U.S. Treasuries, but traders maintained the market's upbeat mood was still intact.
"There is nothing that can change the firm trend in the medium-term," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Activity was quiet most of the session ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting's decision to leave key rates unchanged.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 1/4 to 90-1/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.15 to 125.95.

After the slow activity so far this week waiting for the FOMC meeting to finish, traders said the market was now likely once again to turn its focus to the United States with the important January non-farm payrolls report due for release on Friday.
Even though the market is seen retaining its strong mood, another trader said: "The reality is that at these high levels there is some caution."
He said caution may at the very least hold the market in ranges until the payrolls report is released.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.88 percent from 5.25 percent.
